startScreencast: Experimental tip-of-tree Page command that emits compressed frames through Page.screencastFrame.
Controls format, quality, maxWidth, maxHeight and everyNthFrame.
Current tip-of-tree exposes maxFramesInFlight; frames are bounded until screencastFrameAck is received.
sendLastFrame explicitly trades overall performance for improved latency by retaining/sending the latest produced frame after acknowledgement.
screencastFrame carries base64 compressed image data, metadata and an integer sessionId that is documented as the frame number.
ScreencastFrameMetadata carries scroll/scale/device geometry and a timestamp typed as Network.TimeSinceEpoch.
captureScreenshot: Non-experimental Page.captureScreenshot method is present in the old stable CDP 1.3 subset as well as tip-of-tree.
It is request/response pull capture rather than an event stream.
It supports format, quality, clip and fromSurface; newer tip-of-tree also exposes experimental captureBeyondViewport and optimizeForSpeed parameters.
It returns one base64 image payload per call and has no Page.screencastFrameAck flow-control protocol.

source_level_comparison.continuous_stream_fit: startScreencast is the native event-stream mechanism and exposes explicit in-flight acknowledgement/backpressure controls.
source_level_comparison.compatibility_fit: captureScreenshot has a materially stronger compatibility signal because the method exists in stable 1.3, whereas startScreencast is tip-of-tree experimental.
source_level_comparison.fallback_shape: captureScreenshot can provide deterministic sampled pull capture if screencast capability/version acceptance fails.
source_level_comparison.measurement_boundary: No target-browser FPS, CPU/RSS, latency, encoding cost, drop rate or quality result is established by protocol shape alone.

critical_clock_finding: Page.screencastFrame metadata timestamp is Network.TimeSinceEpoch, not F2's local monotonic clock. It may be retained as an auxiliary source timestamp/clock-domain observation but must not replace captured_monotonic_ns for local ordering without an admitted calibration/uncertainty mapping.
hypothesis: F2 can use capability-negotiated rendered capture: prefer bounded startScreencast on an exact verified browser/CDP build when continuous capture is required, with captureScreenshot as stable-compatible sampled fallback/on-demand capture. Existing PerceptionCaptureBroker remains the bounded local admission/drop authority.
counterhypotheses: Experimental startScreencast may have browser-version bugs or encoding overhead that make sampled captureScreenshot preferable even for continuous observation.
Ack-based flow control may interact poorly with F2 broker drop semantics if adapter acknowledgement is tied to downstream consumption instead of local admission.
captureScreenshot pull cadence may produce lower resource use and sufficient temporal coverage for the actual workloads.
Screencast frame TimeSinceEpoch may have unstable offset relative to F2 monotonic time and should remain auxiliary unless measured calibration is reliable.
next_discriminator: Acquire E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPED and define a capability/version-negotiated rendered-capture policy that preserves broker ownership, bounded backpressure/drop accounting, source-generation fences and monotonic-time authority. Runtime/efficiency promotion requires exact target-browser measurement.
